source.title: Multi-scale Feature Learning Dynamics: Insights for Double Descent
source.authors: M. Pezeshki; Amartya Mitra; Yoshua Bengio; Guillaume Lajoie

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests epoch-wise double descent using a linear teacher-student analysis and experiments, a different method from the original studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-error trajectories over training time and how they vary with regularization and feature-learning scales. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows. The numerical values in the relevant plots are not given in the text.
record.test_reason: The study derives analytical epoch-wise generalization curves for a linear teacher-student model and runs a ResNet18/CIFAR-10 experiment (15% label noise) varying weight decay. Both bear directly on V2 and on the regularization part of V6. This is a different method from the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors view the epoch-wise peak as fast features overfitting before slow features are learned. They state they do not think an interpolation-threshold analogue exists for it.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a replica-method linear teacher-student analysis and a ResNet18 training experiment; the paper focuses on epoch-wise trajectories rather than reproducing the original model-size and data-size sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed curve depends on regularization strength and on the feature-learning scale ratio, represented by κ.

fits_no_version.finding: The theory attributes the epoch-wise peak to disparate learning speeds of feature sets (controlled by κ). The authors argue the epoch-wise peak has no analogue of the interpolation threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epoch-wise double descent arises from superposed bias-variance curves of features learned at different rates, not from crossing an interpolation/effective-complexity threshold.

record.code_released: The text says complete source code is in a GitHub repository and mentions a Colab notebook, but gives no URL.
record.problems: The deep-network evidence is from one reported ResNet18 setup with 15% label noise, and the relevant plot values are not stated in the text. The authors note that the teacher-student model is simple and does not capture finer nonlinear, multilayer network dynamics.

untested.parts: No capacity sweep across model classes.
No test of a single effective-complexity measure. The authors only argue the epoch-wise peak has no interpolation analogue.
Label-noise level is not varied (fixed 15% in ResNet). Multiple peaks are not studied. Optimally tuned regularization is not identified.

missing.what: Large-regularization slice of the heat-maps; the caption says fast features are learned but overfit.
The other two condition numbers in the simulation-vs-theory comparison, where double descent apparently does not appear.

record.verdict_notes: All evidence is figure-only, with no numeric values. Label noise is fixed at 15% in the ResNet run; the analytic main results are presented with σ=λ=0, and the general case is in the appendix.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the epoch-wise pattern across a broad range of deep-network architectures, datasets, or training setups.
No sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
Does not sweep capacity across model classes or test the general capacity-wise curve.
Does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Tests how regularization changes the epoch-wise curve, but does not vary label-noise levels, test multiple peaks, or establish an optimally tuned regularization setting.
Does not recount complexity using an effective number of parameters.

relation.reason: The study reports its own analytical and empirical generalization trajectories and varies conditions governing the appearance of epoch-wise double descent.

tranche.reason: Replica-method teacher-student analysis, numerical validation, and ResNet18 regularization experiments investigate epoch-wise double descent using a different method aimed at the same question.

source_check.notes: The supplied source identifies itself as a December 2021 preprint; ICML 2021 review status is not established. Appendix A also argues against an interpolation-threshold analogue for epoch-wise double descent, relevant to V5 but unrepresented in the listed rows.

statements.correction: ResNet18: CIFAR-10; 15% label noise; Adam learning rate 1e-4; 1K epochs; 50 seeds. Small regularization produces epoch-wise double descent. Teacher-student examples include κ=100. Figure 4 reports error bars over 100 seeds. Source identifies itself as a preprint dated 6 December 2021; code availability is stated.
statements.problem: The experimental claims are supported, but the supplied text does not establish reviewed publication status.

statements.correction: ResNet18/CIFAR-10 with 15% label noise and teacher-student κ=100: intermediate regularization removes the second descent while retaining decrease-then-increase overfitting. Optimal regularization is untested.
statements.problem: The conventional overfitting curve is accurately described, but it does not establish a limitation of V6: intermediate regularization is not shown to be optimal, and V6 does not require monotone risk.
